name: NASTrack
backbones: OSTrack ViT supernets (tiny, small, base; base initialized from MAE ViT-B): NASTrack-T; NASTrack-S; NASTrack-B
main_result: NASTrack-T: LaSOT AUC 64.2 at 1.3 GFLOPs, 62 fps on Jetson Orin NX (OSTrack 69.1 at 21.5 GFLOPs, 18 fps); NASTrack-B 68.6 at 14.8 GFLOPs
notes: [core] Single object tracking: one-shot NAS on an OSTrack-style one-stream ViT where the per-layer token keeping ratio (1, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6) is a search dimension next to depth, width, heads and MLP ratio, so the ratio is fixed per searched subnet and the same for every frame. A blacklist removes keep-ratio patterns whose subnets collapse (low IoU with reasonable Params) and a Token Overlap Ratio picks a distillation teacher from an elite pool. The paper does not say how tokens are scored for pruning (it refers to 'importance scores' and builds on OSTrack, whose candidate elimination uses template attention), so criterion is '?'. Supernets trained 300 epochs on tracking data from MAE-pretrained ViT-B. Speed on RTX 4070 laptop GPU, Jetson Orin NX and i7-14700HX CPU; batch size not stated. Searched keep ratios match EViT and PPT pruning at the same architecture (Table 7).
evidence: "This framework incorporates token pruning to optimize both transformer block structures and the layer-wise token keeping ratio" (Abstract); "We incorporate the keeping ratio into the search space and utilize NAS to automatically find the optimal keeping ratio for each layer." (3.1); "We train the model using the OSTrack [Ye et al., 2022] framework, which adopts the Vanilla ViT-Base [Dosovitskiy et al., 2021] model as the backbone, pre-trained with MAE [He et al., 2022]" (4.1)

name: RCTP
notes: [core] Retraining-free token pruning with per-block thresholds chosen for a FLOPs constraint; evaluation details are unknown. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Token importance is Fisher information (gradient-based). A three-stage pipeline builds a candidate threshold table and a FLOPs-Fisher table, and a modified Viterbi algorithm picks the per-block threshold set with minimum Fisher loss for each FLOPs constraint in one shot. Pruning by threshold suggests the token count varies per image, but the abstract does not say. Datasets, backbones and numbers are not in the abstract. ISCAS paper; no hardware design is mentioned.
evidence: "we introduce Fisher information (FI) from tokens to evaluate token importance across different transformer blocks and propose a Retraining-free Constraint-aware Token Pruning (RCTP) framework" (Abstract); "a modified Viterbi algorithm determines optimal threshold sets with minimum overall FI loss under different FLOPs-constraints in one shot" (Abstract)

name: TinyDrop
backbones: DeiT-S; DeiT-B; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; BEiTv2-L; DeiT3-L (guidance: EfficientFormerV2-S2; EfficientNetV2-rw-t)
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.6 at 1.4 GFLOPs incl. guidance model and early exit (baseline 79.8 at 4.6); ViT-L/16: 85.2 at 9.6 (baseline 85.8 at 61.6)
notes: [core] Training-free token dropping for ViT classification with ImageNet results on DeiT-S and large ViTs. A small CNN or ViT guidance model runs first: if its max softmax confidence c exceeds tau the image exits with the guidance prediction, otherwise a Grad-CAM saliency map from the guidance model, resized to the ViT grid, selects the top-K patch tokens once before the first block of the frozen target ViT (positional embeddings and relative position bias are sliced). Drop ratio r = min(r_max, r_max (c/tau)^gamma) with gamma=0.5, r_max=0.7, so the count depends on the image. Reported GFLOPs are averages that include the guidance forward, the Grad-CAM backward and the early exits; on DeiT-S the early-exit-only ablation (w/o token dropping) already reaches 79.6% at 1.8 GFLOPs, while token dropping alone gives 79.1% at 3.0, so much of the saving comes from the exit. Which guidance model the Table 2 rows use is not stated. No latency; no code link in the paper. Read arXiv v1.
evidence: "we propose TinyDrop, a training-free token dropping framework guided by a lightweight vision model" (Abstract); "We compute token-wise saliency maps for the guidance model Mg by applying Grad-CAM [16] to the feature maps of its final transformer block" (2.1.2); "To adaptively determine the proportion of tokens to discard, we introduce a parametric confidence-to-drop mapping function" (2.1.3); "Low-importance tokens are discarded before the first transformer block of the target ViT" (2. Method)

name: TAVT
main_result: ViT-B/16: CUB-200-2011 top-1 89.8 at 0.33x FLOPs, 50 ms GPU latency (ViT 90.6 at 1.00x, 134 ms); TAVTp 91.1 at 0.43x
notes: [core] Token pruning for fine-grained classification; published at DATE but contains no hardware design. Tokens are ranked by a significance score, the attention score aggregated over heads, and the top-k are kept. The fine-tuned ViT-B/16 is further fine-tuned with random progressive keep counts (n_{i+1} sampled in [(1-p) n_i, n_i], p=0.2), random layer skipping and sandwich-rule in-place distillation, so one model accepts any per-layer token configuration. A multi-objective evolutionary search with FLOPs as the constraint then picks per-layer token counts that are the same for every image (TAVTp: best accuracy, TAVTe: most efficient within 1% of ViT). Latency on one V100 GPU and an i9-9980XE CPU at batch size 8. FGVC only (CUB, Stanford Dogs, Stanford Cars, NABirds); no ImageNet or DeiT-S. Code not mentioned. Read the PDF in the official DATE 2023 proceedings archive.
evidence: "We identify the top-k attentive tokens based on the significance score and retain the highest value tokens based on the pruning scheme." (III.A); "we conduct a multi-objective evolutionary search to find the optimal token pruning scheme that maximizes accuracy and efficiency for the target computational budgets" (III.C); "Then we further fine-tuned the baseline ViT model on our token adaptive framework with a token drop rate set to 0.2." (IV. Experiments)

name: PF2A-ViT
notes: [hardware] Algorithm-accelerator co-design (28 nm ASIC) whose token pruning is one of three compression parts. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. The parameter-free, feature-aware dynamic token pruning (PF2ATP) adjusts the pruning ratio to the complexity of the feature without running subnetworks; the scoring rule is not described. Also Hessian-trace mixed-precision quantization and cluster-regroup weight encoding. Hardware: bitonic-sorter token pruning module, 3D-PE array with reconfigurable 4/8-bit PEs. Headline: up to 3.89x speedup and 5.54x energy efficiency over state-of-the-art ViT accelerators, 2.25 mm2 and 76 mW in 28 nm. Same group as TWDP (yang2025twdp).
evidence: "a parameter-free and feature-aware dynamic token pruning (PF2ATP) strategy is proposed to reduce the dimension of feature maps and dynamically adjust the pruning ratio according to the complexity of the feature without complex execution of subnetworks" (Abstract); "At the hardware level, a token pruning module based on bitonic sorters is designed to fully leverage PF2ATP." (Abstract)

name: TWDP
notes: [hardware] ViT accelerator (28 nm) with token pruning plus N:M weight pruning. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. The token pruning is parameter-free and self-adaptive and skips computation in an image-dependent manner; whether a threshold or another rule sets the per-image count is not said. Weights use Hessian-aware layer-wise N:M pruning, and an overlapping dataflow reduces temporal storage and latency. Headline: 66.1% less weight storage, 2070.9 FPS/W, 1.6x energy efficiency over state-of-the-art architectures with negligible accuracy loss. Same group as PF2A-ViT (zou2025pf2avit).
evidence: "we propose a parameter-free self-adaptive token pruning method to skip redundant computations in an image-dependent manner" (Abstract); "we apply a Hessian-aware layer-wise N:M weight pruning approach to minimize storage overhead, memory access, and computational power consumption" (Abstract)

name: STEM
notes: [hardware] Token pruning used as a defense against adversarial patch attacks, with an accelerator (STEMA). Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Block-wise Selective Fusion fuses redundant tokens and flags suspicious ones; Identify-Prune removes adversarial tokens using multi-head attention statistics. How redundant tokens are chosen for fusion and how many tokens are removed is not said. STEMA adds a Security Core with token fusion, top-k selection and metadata engines (5% of chip area). Headline: robustness up to 4.7x over token pruning methods, 46.8x-105.8x runtime improvement over defense baselines, and up to 71x speedup and 397x energy efficiency for STEMA. Main goal is robustness, not efficiency.
evidence: "Block-wise Selective Fusion (BSF), which fuses redundant tokens and flags suspicious ones, and Identify-Prune (IP), which identifies and prunes adversarial tokens based on multi-head attention statistics" (Abstract); "STEMA includes specialized engines for token fusion, top-k selection, and metadata management, occupying only 5% of chip area" (Abstract)

name: DPP-ViT
main_result: DeiT-B: 47% computation reduction with 0.25% ImageNet top-1 drop
notes: [hardware] Dynamic patch pruning with a reconfigurable accelerator. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Importance of a patch is the column-wise accumulation of the attention map (attention received); block-wise score thresholds make the count depend on the image. Whether the model is fine-tuned is not said. The accelerator changes dataflow and PE structure by pruning-aware row-level reconfiguration. Headline: 47.96x / 4.36x / 1.47x speedup over EdgeCPU, EdgeGPU and ViTCoD.
evidence: "the column-wise accumulations of attention maps are computed and those are used as importance scores" (Abstract); "Through DPP-ViT with block-wise importance score thresholds, our approach considers image-wise difficulties and block-wise sensitivities" (Abstract)

name: JMP
main_result: DeiT-S: 35% fewer FLOPs, more than 45% higher throughput, top-1 0.2 lower (ImageNet)
notes: [core] Per-sample choice between merging and pruning on DeiT-S with ImageNet numbers; full text not read. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Tokens are split into critical and non-critical ones and the similarity between the two groups decides, per sample, whether non-critical tokens are merged or pruned; how critical tokens are scored and how many are kept is not said. No extra trainable parameters, but whether the model is fine-tuned is not said. Absolute DeiT-S accuracy, GFLOPs and throughput (and GPU) are not in the abstract.
evidence: "this work proposes a token compression framework: joint merging and pruning (JMP), which adaptively selects a better token compression strategy based on the similarity between critical tokens and non-critical tokens in each sample" (Abstract); "does not require the introduction of additional trainable parameters" (Abstract)

name: TSMVT
main_result: 30% fewer tokens with higher precision on marine species classification (numbers not in the abstract)
notes: [application] Underwater fine-grained classification for autonomous underwater vehicles. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. A dynamic token filtering mechanism keeps important tokens, merges low-information tokens and discards background tokens; a multihead attention weighting token-selective (MAWTS) module re-weights attention. The scoring rule, schedule, backbone and training are not described. Four marine and three terrestrial datasets.
evidence: "we propose a dynamic token filtering mechanism that effectively retains important tokens, merges low-information tokens, and discards irrelevant background tokens" (Abstract); "With a 30% reduction in tokens, TSMVT achieves superior precision in classifying marine species" (Abstract)

name: LoTM
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.19 at 3.26 GFLOPs (k=40; baseline 79.82 at 4.65)
notes: [core] Training-free local token merging on DeiT with ImageNet results. Candidate pairs are fixed adjacent pairs (z_i, z_{i+1}) for odd i in the token sequence; the top-k pairs by cosine similarity are averaged at layers 4, 7 and 11, k fixed per layer. FLOPs only (fvcore); evaluation batch 128. Compared with ToMe, K-Medoids, DPC-KNN, SiT, Sinkhorn and PatchMerger (trained methods use their reported numbers). No code link. Read the HAL author version (submitted version, CC BY-NC); the published CCIS text was not compared. Same authors as DHTM (haroun2025dhtm), which extends LoTM.
evidence: "we propose LoTM, a Local Token Merging approach where we constrain the merging window to a pair of adjacent tokens only" (Abstract); "Let k be a hyperparameter representing the number of pairs to merge. Given the previous similarity scores, we pick the top-k most similar adjacent token pairs" (4.2); "Our method operates during inference, reducing the number of tokens in a pretrained model where images are initially split into 14×14 tokens, without requiring any additional training." (5.2)

name: DHTM
main_result: DeiT-S: top-1 79.46 at 3.26 GFLOPs (k=40 at layers 4, 7, 11; baseline 79.82 at 4.65)
notes: [core] Training-free local token merging on DeiT with ImageNet results; extends LoTM (haroun2025lotm) from fixed adjacent pairs to any 8-connected neighbours. In each selected layer the most similar (cosine) neighbouring pair is merged by averaging, repeated k times (hierarchical agglomerative clustering in a local form), so k tokens are removed per layer. Default layers {4, 7, 11}; applying it to all layers is better above 39% FLOPs reduction. FLOPs only (fvcore); batch size 1 in evaluation but no latency. No code link. Read the open-access SCITEPRESS PDF (CC BY-NC-ND).
evidence: "we iteratively merge tokens in each layer, fusing a fixed number of selected neighbor token pairs based on their similarity" (Abstract); "Our proposed approach is off-the-shelf, i.e., it does not require additional training." (Abstract); "in each selected layer, we iteratively merge k times, where k is predefined." (4.3)

name: AToM
notes: [hardware] Algorithm-architecture co-design for adaptive token merging. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Merging is image-adaptive and fine-grained; First-Come-First-Merge mapping and Linear Distance Calculation cut the cost of merging and unmerging. The abstract mentions unmerging, so merged tokens are restored at some point (where and why is not said). How the merge count adapts per image (threshold or another rule) is not said. The architecture has dedicated merge and unmerge engines in an end-to-end pipeline. Headline: average end-to-end speedups of 10.9x, 7.7x, 5.4x and energy savings of 24.9x, 1.8x, 16.7x over CPU, EdgeGPU and GPU; 1.2x-1.9x higher effective throughput than existing transformer accelerators.
evidence: "The AToM algorithm employs an image-adaptive, fine-grained merging strategy, significantly boosting computational efficiency." (Abstract); "We also optimize the merging and unmerging processes to minimize overhead, employing techniques like First-Come-First-Merge mapping and Linear Distance Calculation." (Abstract)

name: FTCFormer
main_result: FTCFormer: ImageNet-1k top-1 77.9 at 4.1 GFLOPs (TCFormer 77.5 at 3.8, PVT 75.1 at 1.9)
notes: [out-of-scope?] Clustering replaces grid downsampling between stages of a hierarchical transformer to improve accuracy, not to cut cost: the token count is always N/4 per stage and FLOPs rise over TCFormer. Cluster centers come from density peaks clustering with fuzzy KNN on token features (top N/4 of rho x delta), other tokens are assigned by a shared-nearest-neighbour score, and each cluster is merged with channel-wise importance weights from a linear layer, followed by cross-attention to the original tokens. Trained from scratch (300 epochs on ImageNet); 32 classification datasets. No latency.
evidence: "we propose Fuzzy Token Clustering Transformer (FTCFormer), which incorporates a novel clustering-based downsampling module to dynamically generate vision tokens based on the semantic meanings instead of spatial positions" (Abstract); "with the top N/4 scoring tokens (equivalent to 2× downsampling) chosen to maintain hierarchical consistency with standard vision Transformer architectures" (3.2.1); "for ImageNet-1k [10] we train the model using three A100 GPUs with the learning rate 0.001, batch size 120 for 300 epochs" (4.1)

name: TREWA
notes: [core] Wavelet-based token reduction for ViTs with comparisons to pruning methods; full text not read. Only the abstract was available (from the record in the authors' institutional repository iris.univpm.it; the PDF there needs a login, Springer blocked automated access, no arXiv copy), so the values below rest on the abstract. A DWT is applied to the token embeddings and only the low-frequency coefficients go to the next attention layer, dropping 50-75% of the tokens; the new tokens are DWT coefficients rather than a subset or average of the old ones, so operation is 'other'. For each image the level is chosen by comparing its attention entropy with that of the batch. Four datasets, pre-trained and from-scratch settings (whether the pre-trained setting is fine-tuned is not said).
evidence: "It then applies the DWT to the token embeddings and forwards only the low-frequency coefficients (i.e., those capturing the image’s main semantic structure) to the next attention layer, discarding 50–75% of the tokens." (Abstract); "For each image in a batch, TREWA selects a pruning level by comparing that image’s attention entropy with the batch one." (Abstract); "We evaluate TREWA on four benchmark datasets in both pre-trained and training from scratch settings" (Abstract)

name: CAMixerSR
main_result: CAMixerSR-B: Test8K PSNR 33.81 dB at 1.49 GFLOPs (gamma=0.5; 33.81 at 1.96 GFLOPs with gamma=1)
notes: [out-of-scope?] Image super-resolution network, not a ViT, and no token leaves the sequence: a learned predictor scores each 16x16 window, the top-K windows (ratio gamma=0.5) get deformable window self-attention and the rest only a cheap convolution path with spatial attention. Gumbel-softmax mask in training, argsort top-K at inference; a ratio loss controls gamma (pre-trained with gamma_ref=0.5, fine-tuned with gamma_ref in [0, 1]). Trained from scratch on DIV2K (500k iterations). Also lightweight SR and omnidirectional SR. FLOPs only.
evidence: "we propose a content-aware mixer (CAMixer) to route token mixers with different complexities according to the content" (1. Introduction); "During inference, by descending sorting mask m with argsort(m), we obtain the index Ihard of top K related windows for sparse attention" (3.1); "The AdamW [24] is adopted with the initial learning rate 5×10−4 and 500k iterations training procedure." (4.1)

name: STP + MTA
main_result: ViT-B + UNETR: BraTS DSC 75.79 at 7.79 img/s encoder throughput (r=0.75; UNETR 75.44 at 4.85)
notes: [application] 3D medical image segmentation (BTCV CT, MSD BraTS MRI) with a ViT-B encoder and UNETR decoder. Soft-topK Token Pruning: an MLP sub-network scores tokens and keeps the top K = (1 - r) n at blocks 3, 6 and 9 (straight-through Gumbel top-K in training, plain top-K at inference). Multi-layer Token Assembly then puts the pruned intermediate tokens (with block tokens) back with the output tokens and runs Transformer blocks before the decoder. Trained with the segmentation loss only; whether the ViT-B starts from pre-trained weights is not said, so training is '?'. Throughput on one A100 at batch size 1; training throughput also rises (up to 120%). Read arXiv v1 (12 pages, the IPMI text was not compared).
evidence: "STP predicts token importance scores with a lightweight sub-network and samples the topK tokens" (Abstract); "In token completion, MTA restores a full token sequence by assembling both sparse output tokens and pruned multi-layer intermediate ones." (Abstract); "Three STP modules are inserted after the 3rd, 6th, and 9th Transformer blocks in ViT-B." (3.2)

name: ESTJ
main_result: 75% higher throughput, 40% fewer GFLOPs and up to 1.1 higher mIoU (backbone and dataset not in the abstract)
notes: [core] Token merging for ViT semantic segmentation; full text not read. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. Hierarchical Condition Pooling merges tokens in hierarchical local windows and Protected Bipartite Matching protects informative tokens (high average similarity to all other tokens) during global bipartite merging. A merging threshold can be changed at inference. How the merged tokens are restored for the segmentation head, the backbones, datasets and training are not in the abstract.
evidence: "ESTJ merges tokens using two strategies: Hierarchical Condition Pooling (HCP), which employs hierarchical local windows to effectively select sufficient tokens, and Protected Bipartite Matching (PBM), designed to preserve informative tokens using average similarity between a token and all other tokens" (Abstract); "ESTJ can adjust the merging threshold during inference to adapt to scenarios that prioritize efficiency or accuracy" (Abstract)

name: FR2ViT
main_result: Segmenter ViT-L: 1.95x FPS with 0.43% performance drop
notes: [core] Finetuning-free token reduction for dense prediction; full text not read. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. A high-order informativeness assessment splits tokens into superior and inferior ones; superior tokens get full attention ('refinement') and inferior tokens are processed by a cheaper reactivation branch, with light interaction between the branches, so every token stays active at a different cost. The scoring rule, the split ratio, the three dense tasks and other backbones are not in the abstract.
evidence: "we propose FR2ViT, a finetuning-free refinement-reactivation architecture for efficient vision transformers, allowing tokens of varying informativeness to activate softly at differing costs" (Abstract); "We refine superior tokens through extensive attention interaction, while inferior tokens undergo effective reactivation" (Abstract)

name: TaskTP
main_result: Mask R-CNN: COCO 31.4 to 38.5 fps; ScanNet object search 3197 ms to 2437 ms
notes: [application] Robotics perception: token pruning conditioned on the set of object categories a task needs. Only the publisher abstract (via OpenAlex) was available: the article is paywalled and no arXiv or repository copy was found, so the values below rest on the abstract alone and the rest is '?'. A dynamic gating network between Transformer blocks scores each token's relevance to the target category set; fewer categories allow more pruning. One task-agnostic training phase, then any category subset is configured at deployment without retraining (whether the backbone is fine-tuned is not said). Accuracy numbers and the transformer backbone are not in the abstract.
evidence: "A dynamic gating network is introduced between successive Transformer blocks, which evaluates the relevance of each token to the given task." (Abstract); "After a task-agnostic training phase, it can be flexibly configured at deployment time to support any category subset without retraining" (Abstract)

name: ToDo
main_result: DreamShaper v7: up to 4.5x faster at 2048x2048; at 1536x1536 MSE to baseline 6.2e-3 (ToMe 2.7e-2) at merge ratio 0.75
notes: [out-of-scope?] Four-page IJCAI demo paper: keys and values of the U-Net self-attention are downsampled on the 2D grid by nearest-neighbour (strided) subsampling, while all queries are kept, so the output sequence is not shortened (closer to sparse attention than to token reduction). Fixed downsampling (merge ratio 0.75 = 2x, 0.89 = 3x, 0.9375 = 4x), applied without training. Evaluation: 10 generations per setting on one A6000 (fp16, flash attention, DDIM 50 steps), MSE and high-pass-filter magnitude against the baseline, no FID. No code link (demo video only). Read the IJCAI proceedings PDF.
evidence: "We propose a novel training-free method ToDo that relies on token downsampling of key and value tokens to accelerate Stable Diffusion inference" (Abstract); "we employ a downsampling function D(·) using the Nearest-Neighbor algorithm" (2.2); "This modification entails the application of the downsampling operation D(·) to the keys, K, and values V of the attention mechanism while preserving the original queries Q." (2.2)
